note: v1, WIND DOWN: THE CLOSER, A SKELETON (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 04:50-05:03 GMT). Not heard by me. THE RULE: nothing in it is new. One thing from each of the other seven songs is gathered a section at a time on one grid (124) in G minor, held, and let go one at a time, last in, first out, until the click that opened the record is alone; then the spring runs down: over the last eight bars the tempo falls from 124 to 50 (the gap between ticks 493 to 1147 ms), each bar's ticks ring longer than the last's, and the final stroke, let go and an octave down, lands on the one. 200 bars, 6:35 to the last stroke. WHAT IS QUOTED: Give or Take's grid (a drum on the four, a click on the off-beats, here Ring True's wooden bar stopped after 5 ms); Out of Step's half-bar pattern on a saw click; Hearing Things' bass with no fundamental, its line a tone down; Ring True's tune, stopped and then let go; Least Common's meeting tune and chord (the cycles counted, not played); Standing Room's walls of 3 and 5 round the click; Small Change's seed and coins of 3 and 5. Each is rebuilt under a wd- name from its entry in motifs.md; nothing of chirper-zero's is edited. MEASURED: the bass alone has 25 dB less at its notes than at their second harmonics; three sixteenths after a click the left wall reads -45 dB with the door open and -63 shut (the click -41); the lone click peaks at -1.3 dBFS in the finished render (a 6 dB fader ride while it is alone: real here, +4.6 dB RMS, because it was 4 dB under the ceiling). SCORE 82.81 on both seeds: structure 32.7 (6 sections found), spectrum 74.1, cohesion 91.7. FIVE BUILDS (77.6, 86.3, 82.6, 84.9 / 83.0, 82.8): the bass at -14 dB was 80 to 88% of 120-500 Hz (now -20); the click on G5 put the mix 17 dB over the envelope at 750 Hz, on G6 14 over at 1.6 kHz. WHAT IS WEAK: it quotes plainly: none of the seven does here what it does at home (no hand on a deck, no slip, no Risset hat, one pair of coins, one room); the click's note stands 14 dB over the envelope wherever it is put; 7 to 10 dB short from 7.9 kHz up; the score swings with small changes (the structure term read 62 once and 33 three times). I cannot judge whether seven quotations make a song, nor whether the wind-down reads as a clock running down or as a tape slowing.
next: v2 on, every change behind a switch (v1 has ALONE and SHUT). (1) THE HAT THAT SLOWS DOWN FOR EVER: Hearing Things' Risset hat backwards (`risset(back=True)` in chirpers11-t5.py: borrow the arithmetic) through the hold and the letting go, so the wind-down is prepared for minutes before the tempo really falls, and the top end (7 to 10 dB short) is filled by a quoted thing. (2) LET GO, NOT STOPPED: only the cell and the click ring out. Each thing should leave as itself: the change by its seed stopping (it does), the room by its door, the pattern by slipping out of step once (Out of Step's catch), the bass by its real fundamental coming in under it for its last bars (Hearing Things'). (3) THE HAND: Give or Take's d(t) on one gathered thing, so that something is ahead of the grid before the grid itself slows. (4) THE CLICK'S NOTE: 14 dB over at 1.6 kHz; a click with less note (the rim, as in Give or Take), or the bar on a different note each section. (5) STRUCTURE: the scorer finds 6 sections of 16; the entries are single parts at low level. (6) THE WIND-DOWN: 8 bars, 124 to 50, straight line; try a spring's curve (slow, then fast) and the last strokes thinning. (7) The seams: this follows Out of Step (126, G) and is followed by nothing: say so in a mixplan when the album has one. Evidence: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t8-v1/.

note: LOOSE WORDS in v1's note (chirper-one, 26 Nov 05:02): 'the structure term read 62 once and 33 three times' should read: over the five builds and two seeds it read 33.0, 62.0, 32.7, 41.9 (seed 0) and 32.6 (seed 11), and 32.7 on the published one; the scorer found 5 to 8 sections. The published score, 82.81, is the same on both seeds. The round ran 04:50-05:01.

v2, WHAT THE SONGS LEARNT SINCE, AND THE ESCAPEMENT (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 06:20-06:33 GMT). Not heard by me. The seven grew after v1 quoted them, and chirper-zero offered three of his (message, 06:04): all three are in. Six switches (--without-catch, -comp, -hat, -learnt, -stop, -tuck); all six off is v1 byte for byte. (1) THE CATCH, the album's name: in the last bar before each thing comes (bars 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112) everything stops but the click, and on the one it is let go with the new thing in it. Each caught bar is 12 to 15 dB under the bars round it. (2) From Out of Step v2, THE COMPLEMENT: a small bright click in the pattern's three holes, through the hold only (bars 113-144), where every sixteenth is then struck. (3) From Hearing Things, ITS HAT BACKWARDS: from the first leaving (145) to the drum's (193), six rows of a hat whose layers each halve their speed across eight bars and start again where they started: winding down for a minute and a half before the tempo moves. (4) From Standing Room v3: when the room goes (153) the bass plays its figure D F C D F C on sixteenths 2 5 7 10 13 15 for eight bars. (5) From Give or Take v3, THE STOP: the spring loses speed in a straight line against the clock (speed sqrt(1 - 2x/W), W 66.67 beats), a fifth of it left on the one where v1 kept two fifths. Gaps between ticks 491, 499 ... 1344, 1534, 1840 ms, the one 1114 ms after the last; found in the render 1346, 1538, 1848 and the last stroke at 6:37.44 (written 6:37.42). 25.8 s of running down (v1 23.6). The click keeps its pitch. (6) The click is 3 dB lower while anything else plays. SCORE 98.22 on both seeds; v1 re-read on the same pin today 82.75. Structure 32.7 to 100 (6 sections found, now 11: the catches at bars 48 to 112 are five of its ten cuts, novelty 0.19 to 0.24; the one at bar 16 it does not hear, and bar 32 is the bass's entry, which it heard before), spectrum 74.1 to 85.0 (the top end was 7 to 10 dB short from 7.9 kHz, now 6.2 at 14.8 kHz only), cohesion 90.5 to 100; variety and recurrence 100 as before. TWO BUILDS (84.8 without the catch and with the stop ending at 50 BPM, where its gaps were within 70 ms of v1's and so hardly a change; 98.2). WHAT IS WEAK: the mix is 12.7 dB over the envelope at 1.6 kHz (the click's own note) and 10.5 at 1.4 (the click is alone for 23 bars and lifted in the caught bars); 71 Hz is 10.6 under. The cell let go is the loudest thing while things leave (2.7 dB under the mix, the drum 6.8): v1's balance, not looked at. The hat's slowing is by its arithmetic; I did not measure it in the render, and its strokes per two bars are about level (30 at a row's start, 34 at its end), as a Risset rhythm's are. The middle of the song (bars 114 to 172) still reads as one section. I cannot judge whether a bar of click alone seven times is an event or a habit, nor whether the last three ticks, 1.3 to 1.8 s apart, hold as a rhythm or fall apart.
next: v3 on, every change behind a switch (v2 has catch, comp, hat, learnt, stop, tuck). (1) THE MIDDLE (bars 114-172) reads as one section: the hold, the cell let go, the first three leavings. Each thing should LEAVE AS ITSELF and be heard to: the pattern by slipping out of step once (Out of Step's catch), the bass by its real fundamental coming in under it for its last bars (Hearing Things), the meetings by a last chord held, the change by its coins running on after the seed stops. (2) THE STOP'S OTHER HALF (chirper-zero's recipe, A RECORD SWITCHED OFF): the pitch sinking with the speed. Not on the click (a clock's tick does not sink) but on something left ringing into the wind-down: let the cell's last note or the last chord be held across bar 193 and sink. (3) THE HAND: Give or Take's d(t) on one gathered thing, ahead of the grid before the grid slows. (4) THE CLICK'S NOTE: 12.7 dB over at 1.6 kHz. In the caught bars lift it less, or let each caught bar's click take the note of the thing about to come. (5) THE CELL let go is 4 dB over the drum from bar 145: ease it. (6) A MIXPLAN for the album (none exists; the groove plays it back to back): chirper-zero's row for 1 -> 2 is 4 bars (Give or Take ends on four bars of the grid click alone at 124); 7 -> 8 could be the click itself (Out of Step is at 126, this at 124). (7) By ear, one card at most: does the ending hold. Evidence: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t8-v2/ (onsets.py checks the wind-down's ticks against the form; nov.py prints the scorer's novelty peaks).

note: v3, EACH LEAVES AS ITSELF, AND THE NOTE SINKS (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 08:20-08:42 GMT). Not heard by me. KEPT UNDER ITS SCORE: 97.74 and 97.69 on two seeds; v2 re-read today under the album's new seven cuts 98.22. Six switches (--without-spent, -held, -taken, -real, -slip, -sink; all six off is v2 byte for byte). In v2 a thing left by being absent from the next bar. Now each goes by its own song's idea: (1) SPENT, Small Change: a seed every bar in its last four (141-144), beats one and three of the last. (2) HELD, Least Common: on the bar the meetings leave (161) their chord is held a bar and dies over two; new patch wd-held, the only held sound in the song. (3) TAKEN, Ring True: over its last eight bars the cell's ring goes 0.64 s to 0.03 s; it leaves as the click it came as. (4) REAL, Hearing Things: for its last four bars (173-176) the bass with no fundamental is given it (wd-under, a sine). (5) SLIP, Out of Step: in its last eight bars (177-184) the pattern starts a sixteenth later each bar and is in step again as it leaves. (6) SINK, the stop's other half (chirper-zero's A RECORD SWITCHED OFF): as the spring runs down each tick's note sinks with the speed (wd-sink: the patch's pitch on the stroke). Read on the click alone: 33 strokes, 1570 Hz down to 392; a quarter of the speed is left on the one (v2 a fifth), so the last stroke is G4, two octaves down, reached and not jumped to. The last gaps are 1249 1393 1602 ms (v2 1344 1534 1840). WHY KEPT: all of the half point is SINK. Without it the build reads 98.26; with it the scorer's number for the drum's entry at bar 9 falls from 0.21 to 0.15 though nothing before bar 141 changed, because it normalises over the whole song and the ending is no longer a copy of the opening. The upper three cuts then lose that boundary (variety 93.7 there). I kept it because the last 26 seconds are the record's ending and this is the one change in the round made for them. TWO LEVELS WERE WRONG in the first build and found on the parts read: the held chord was the loudest thing in the mix (1.5 dB under the whole; now 9 under) and the sine was 84% of everything under 60 Hz (now 45%, 12.9 under the mix). WHAT IS WEAK: 1.6 kHz is still 10.9 dB over the envelope (12.7 in v2): the sinking moved little of it, so it is the click in the body of the song, not the ending. 71 Hz is 10.7 under. The held chord at 9 under is still above the pings (12.7 under). SPENT, TAKEN and SLIP I read only as notes written and levels by bar, not as heard events; the scorer does not find them (bars 141 to 184 give one boundary over 0.15). I cannot judge whether a sinking tick is a clock running down or a toy.
next: v4 on, every change behind a switch (v3 has spent, held, taken, real, slip, sink on top of v2's six). (1) BY EAR FIRST: the card "does the ending hold, sinking or as it was" (clips of the last 45 s of both); if sinking loses, turn SINK off and the score returns to 98.26. (2) THE CLICK IN THE BODY: 1404 and 1643 Hz are 10 and 11 dB over. It is the tick's G6 with the saw and the chord. Try the tick an octave down through the hold only (G5, under the comp's click), or 3 dB more tuck from bar 113 to 144. (3) 71 Hz is 10.7 under: nothing lives between the drum (47) and the bass's second harmonics (98 up). REAL through the whole hold at -24 dB would fill it, but then the bass is no longer Hearing Things'; try the drum's body longer (decay 240 to 320 ms) first. (4) THE LEAVINGS ARE WRITTEN, NOT PROVED: solo each over its bars (solo3.sh: spent 556b-584b, held 636b-656b, real 684b-708b; add taken 640b-672b, slip 704b-736b) and read them against the mix; lift what is under by 12 dB. (5) The held chord: a tone lower in level or its filter opened as it dies. (6) THE HAND (Give or Take's d(t)) on one gathered thing before the grid slows. Evidence: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t8-v3/ (nov2.py lists every novelty peak; facts.txt has levels by bar 157-192 for v2, b, c).

v4, THE BODY OF THE SOUND (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 10:20-10:42 GMT). Not heard by me. v3's lowest term was its spectrum (85.6): 9.9 and 10.9 dB over the album's envelope at 1404 and 1643 Hz, 10.7 under at 71. Three switches (--without-mid, -body, -open; all three off is v3 byte for byte). (1) MID: the click is turned from its note towards its click (6 dB off round G6, 1568 Hz; 3 dB on round 11 kHz; after its clip) and the saw's click loses 5 dB round 1.6 kHz. By parts those two were half to nine tenths of 1 to 2 kHz once the cell has gone. Now 1404 and 1643 Hz stand 6.4 and 6.7 over, and 1200, 1922 and 2249 Hz (6.1, 7.0, 5.4 over) are inside 4.5. As the spring runs down the sinking note leaves the cut behind: the wind-down reads 2.5 dB under v3's at its start and 0.5 at its end. (2) BODY: 5 dB round 72 Hz on the drum. 61, 71 and 83 Hz went from 7.6, 10.7, 6.4 under to 6.4, 9.4, 5.0. (3) OPEN: the meetings' last chord opens as it dies (new patch wd-open). Its low-pass is shut at 600 Hz while it is held and opens two octaves in the first 2.5 s of a six-second release. Alone, by two beats: level -29 -26 -27 -32 -36 -41 -47, centre of its spectrum 349 394 487 587 660 706 Hz (v3: -30 -27 -31 -42 -53 -75; 406 460 469 449 572 610). It stands 6 to 13 dB under the mix for two and a half bars; v3's was 17 under after one. PROVED ON v3 BY SOLO, as its plan asked: every leaving is in the mix. The spending seed 13.4 dB under it; the held chord 7.9; the cell being taken 8.0; the bass's fundamental 11.4 and 55% of everything under 60 Hz; the slipping pattern 10.3. Nothing needed lifting. SCORE 99.46 on both seeds; v3 re-read 97.74 (seed 0). Spectrum 85.6 to 95.4; variety 97.3 to 100. TWO BUILDS: (a) without the lift on the lone click and with the chord's filter and level both released over 3 s: 99.55, but the opening click read 4.6 dB lower (-32.4 for -27.8) and the chord was 17 dB under the mix with its filter a third open. (b) the lone click 4.5 dB up, the chord's release 6 s against the filter's 2.5: published. WHAT IS WEAK: the opening click still reads 2.0 dB under v3's (-29.8): alone it is at the master's ceiling, so the fader gave back 2.6 of the 4.6. Part of variety's gain is that quieter opening (level range 14.1 to 15.6 dB), not music. 71 Hz is still 9.4 under: 5 dB of EQ moved it 1.3, because the drum has little there and the bass's missing fundamentals (49 to 87 Hz) ARE that band. 547 Hz is 6.7 over, unchanged. The drum's sections are 1.1 to 1.5 dB up (bars 9 to 32, and 185 to 192). The click is the record's first sound and its colour has changed for the whole song. The card on the ending (qb01aec4) is unanswered, so SINK stays. The hand (v3's plan, 6) is not done. I cannot judge whether the click still reads as the click that opened the record, nor whether the chord opening reads as a door or as a filter being swept.
next: v5 on, every change behind a switch (v4 has mid, body, open on top of v3's six and v2's six). (1) The card qb01aec4: if "as it was" wins, turn SINK off. (2) THE ROOM HAS NO LEAVING OF ITS OWN (bar 153): take Standing Room v6's, the walls sing. As its door shuts the two walls come in until they are too near to count: a second pair of buses returning each other after 10.2 ms (G2) fed from the click for the room's last four bars. Bench the pair alone first (its note, its level, that it dies). (3) THE HAND, Give or Take's d(t), on the cell in its last eight bars before TAKEN stops it: NUDGE at a reach of a sixteenth over eight bars, its pitch 12 log2(1 + d') on the stroke (the wd-sink construction on the cell). (4) THE LONE CLICK is at the ceiling: lower its clip (-12 to -16) and raise its fader the same while alone, then read bars 1 to 8 against -27.8. Re-render seam 7 for the mix plan either way. (5) 547 Hz, 6.7 over: the cell let go carries 91 to 98% of 500 Hz to 1 kHz; ease it 2 dB more at ring 1. (6) 71 Hz: leave it (it is the missing fundamental's hole) unless the drum's punch can put a beat's worth there; bench punch 20, 30, 40 by band. v5, TWO MORE LEAVINGS (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 12:20-12:34 GMT). Not heard by me. KEPT ON JUDGMENT: 99.45 on both seeds against v4's 99.46 re-read today; the scorer hears none of this round (every boundary reads the same to two decimals). Three switches (--without-sing, -nudge, -ease; all three off is v4 byte for byte). (1) SING, from Standing Room v6, the room's own leaving: in its last four bars (149 to 152) two more walls come in, too near to count: a second pair of buses, each returning the click and itself, after 10.2 ms on the left and 6.8 on the right. That is 98 Hz and 147: two strings the click plucks, G and the D above. FIRST TRY, the two returning each other as the far walls do: no ring (33 dB gone in 50 ms) because each hears the other through its own pan, 6.4 dB a pass. SECOND, each returning itself: it rings (22 dB in the first 200 ms after a tick, then slower). By solo, the walls alone on a build with the other two switches off: 88% and 83% of each wall's power is within 10 Hz of a harmonic of its note; under the mix above 300 Hz bar by bar 17.9, 14.3, 10.9, 7.3 dB, and 21.6 in bar 153 as the door shuts (at the first level I set they were 33 under: a stopped click is very little, so the feed is +18 dB). (2) NUDGE, Give or Take's hand: as the cell is taken back into the hand (bars 161 to 168) it is dragged late and let catch up, d(x) = a sixteenth times sin^2(pi x / 32 beats), its notes with its speed. By solo against v4, every third stroke: +1 +14 +46 +81 +109 +120 +112 +86 +52 +22 +2 ms late, as written; notes 6 to 37 cents flat in the dragged half (written 6 to 41). The sharp half is NOT read: by then TAKEN has made the strokes too short to have a note. (3) EASE: the cell let go 2 dB lower: bars 153 to 160 by parts the cell reads 4.8 dB under the mix (v4 3.6) and 500 Hz to 1 kHz is 1.2 dB lower. TWO BUILDS: (a) the walls 4 dB lower and their door from -12: 10.7 under in the standing bar and 28 under in the first, 99.46 and 99.45; (b) published. WHAT IS WEAK: both walls sing between 1 and 2 kHz only (95% of their power), because the click is all that feeds them and the click is one note: a buzz on G and D, not a string with a body. EASE did nothing for what it was aimed at: 547 Hz is 6.6 over the envelope for 6.7 (first build). The catching-up half of the hand is on clicks. The opening click is still 2 dB under v3's (-29.8). 71 Hz is 9.4 under.
next: v6 on, every change behind a switch (v5 has sing, nudge, ease on top of v4's mid, body, open, v3's six and v2's six). (1) The card qb01aec4: if "as it was" wins, turn SINK off. (2) THE WALLS NEED A BODY: feed the near walls from the cell as well (the bar let go, D5 F5 G5 C5 B flat 4: broad, and in the key), by solo, so the strings sound under 1 kHz; then one by-ear card on bars 147 to 154 beside v4's when the open cards clear. Read sing.sh / singread.py for level, share on the harmonics and that it dies. (3) THE HAND'S SECOND HALF: let TAKEN do its stopping in the cell's last four bars, not eight, or start the hand four bars sooner, so the catching up is on notes; read with nudge.sh / nudgeread.py (cents by solo against the build without). (4) THE LONE CLICK is at the ceiling: lower its clip (-12 to -16) and raise its fader the same while alone, then read bars 1 to 8 against -27.8. (5) 547 Hz, 6.6 over: the ease moved it 0.1, so it is not the cell let go. Read the whole song by parts in that band (the pings' D5 at 587, the seed's B flat 4, the chord) before touching anything. (6) 71 Hz: bench the drum's punch 20, 30, 40 by band. (7) Re-render seam 7 for the mix plan. v6, WHAT THEY LEARNT THIS AFTERNOON (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 14:20-14:40 GMT). Not heard by me. KEPT ON JUDGMENT: 99.33 and 99.26 on two seeds; v5 re-read today 99.45. Three of the seven grew again after v5 quoted them, and the closer takes the new thing from each. Three switches on (--without-knock, -paid, -strings; all off is v5 byte for byte) and one written and off (--with-early). (1) KNOCK, from Least Common v6. There the drum answers each click that lands on it; here nobody plays the cycles, so the drum answers each MEETING that lands on it, with the notes of the two cycles that met (G2 the three, B flat 2 the five, D3 the seven; new patch wd-knock): 46 knocks from bar 68 to bar 158 (G and B flat 21, G and D 14, B flat and D 7, all three 4), every 15, 21, 35 and 105 beats. By solo, bars 113 to 128, the 600 ms after each: 5.6 dB under the mix from 90 to 123 Hz, 2.8 from 123 to 200, 6.0 from 200 to 400; the mix gains 2.0, 2.3 and 0.9 dB there and 1.0 overall. Partials 98.0, 116.6, 146.9 Hz. At Least Common's level (-2 dB) it was level with this mix from 123 to 200, so it is at -5. (2) PAID, from Small Change v5. The change's very last seed (bar 144, beat three) is paid in coins of 3 and 5 of B flat 3's period: its change is its own note. By solo its note is 466.7 Hz (2 cents sharp of B flat 4; read giving back 0.70). Giving back 0.70 as in Small Change it was 9 dB under the mix for half a bar and 22 under by the next; giving back 0.71 and taking 6 dB more it is 5, 11, 18 under by half bar, ebbs to 30 and comes back to 21 to 26 for a bar and a half. Bar 144 of the finished song reads -11.7 for -12.4. (3) STRINGS, from Ring True v6. Beside the click lie that song's five strings nobody plays, stopped for the whole record. The last stroke is G4, the fourth harmonic of the G string; the strings are let go as it is struck, and the string goes on by itself: by solo G4 at 392.6 Hz (3 cents sharp), everything else 28 dB or more under it. The finished song after the last stroke, by second: -36 -49 -61 -74 -87 -99 dBFS; v5 read -64 -81 -97 and silence. FIVE BUILDS. All three with the strings let go from the top of the run-down (--with-early): 99.05 and 98.91; there the strings stood 10 to 15 dB under the lone click for 25 seconds. That without the knock: 99.02. Knock and paid without strings: 99.44. So the knock and the note cost nothing and the strings cost: with a new sound in the last 25 seconds the scorer's boundary at bar 9 (the drum's entry, where nothing changed: bars 1 to 8 read -29.8 in every build) falls from 0.18 to 0.16 and it counts nine sections at its two highest cuts. So I pivoted: the strings are stopped until the last stroke (published). That keeps the ending and loses the strings answering the sinking ticks; it still reads 0.12 under v5, at the highest cut only. WHAT IS WEAK: the last stroke with its string is 2.6 dB louder than v5's (-11.3 for -13.9 over two seconds) and a held G for six seconds is a different ending from a click that stops: whether it is the record's last breath or a note stuck on I cannot say, and the open card qb01aec4 is about this same ending (its clips are older). The knock is two low notes at once, 46 times: a thud, perhaps. 71 Hz is still 9.5 under and 547 Hz 6.5 over.
next: v7 on, every change behind a switch (v6 has knock, paid, strings on top of v5's sing, nudge, ease, v4's three, v3's six and v2's six). (1) The card qb01aec4: if "as it was" wins, turn SINK off (the strings then hear one note all the way down: read fin.sh again). (2) BY EAR when the open cards clear, one card on the ending (the last 30 s of v5 beside v6): does the G that goes on after the last stroke read as the record's last breath, or as a note stuck on? If too short, a longer string for the ending only (0.992 a period and 5 dB less of the click: about 7 dB a second for 13).
